name: VWF Vegas Heavyweight Championship
caption: Classy Joey Boy's long-held title, lost to Randall Crane in a Stretcher match at the wing's own Birthday Bash special; Crane defended it against Classy Joey Boy again at Vegas Violence III before losing it back to him in a No Disqualification match on Firestorm 10-28-03, Classy Joey Boy's third reign. That reign was declared vacant on Firestorm (26 February 2004) after an unseen attacker left the champion hospitalized, co-owner Rob Beauty announcing a Gauntlet tournament to crown his successor.
epitaph: The wing's own top title, defended in falls-count-anywhere and Stretcher-match stipulations across its attested run; its third Classy Joey Boy reign ended in vacancy after an in-storyline attack rather than a defense.

name: VWF 24 Hour Championship
caption: The promotion's top title from its first months, won by Sebastian in a one-night tournament in August 2001 and passed through Kerry Powell, Sebastian again, Jack Spade and Zell Strife to Demonic by December 2001. Scott Starring's title through the summer of 2003, taken by Daniel Sinz on a rope-assisted sunset flip that September; Sinz defended it through Vegas Violence III and Firestorm 10-21-03 before losing it to Yancy "Y2K" Kilpatrick in a 24 Hour/Submission title-for-title match on Firestorm 10-28-03. Kilpatrick's reign ended in vacancy after his death, narrated in-fiction as a plane crash; Thunder Valenkov is already billed as champion by the 12 Days Tournament's own Day Twelve broadcast, retaining against Sonicman on the wing's own Kickoff Card the following January, against The Maquilladora in a ladder match on Firestorm (19 January 2004), and against Lance Voltar in an I Quit match at Ghost Town Blues (19 February 2004).
epitaph: A liberally-defended title, contested in falls-count-anywhere matches and open to challengers from the promotion's own 24 Hour division.

name: VWF Tag Team Championship
caption: First won by Demonic and Blaze in the promotion's Tag Team Title Tournament of October 2001; Dage took Blaze's half in Rage In The Cage, and Triple X won the titles that November. The Rhombus's title, briefly held by Randall Crane and Classy Joey Boy that September before The Rhombus regained it when Classy Joey Boy turned on his own partner, then lost it for good to the Rodeo Boys at Vegas Violence III. The title changed hands again at some undocumented point before the 12 Days Tournament's own Day Twelve, when El Gringo Loco and Jushin Liger GOLD are first billed as champions; they retained against the debuting Fallen Angels on the wing's own Kickoff Card the following January. Loco's own outgoing partner Jushin Liger GOLD then lost his half of the title in a four-way ladder match on Firestorm (19 January 2004), Billy Bones claiming the second belt to form a new pairing with Loco. The new pairing retained without a decision against Hot Property on Firestorm (26 February 2004) after the referee stopped the match over an unidentified man's ringside appearance.
epitaph: A tag title that changed hands off-page between two attested reigns; the surviving record does not show the actual title match. A second, undocumented change of hands followed before the wing's own 12 Days Tournament finale, and a third change split one outgoing pairing's own two belts between two different men in a single ladder match.

name: VWF Submission Championship
caption: A new title created for a five-man qualifying tournament run across September 2003; Yancy "Y2K" Kilpatrick won the tournament final at Vegas Violence III to become its first champion, then lost it to Daniel Sinz that November during the wing's own 12 Days Tournament. A challenge from "Maniac" Mike Wolfe at Ghost Town Blues (19 February 2004) ended without a decision when the presumed-dead Kilpatrick reappeared alive mid-match; Sinz retains by default.
epitaph: Crowned by a submission-only qualifying tournament at Vegas Violence III; its first champion also went on to unify it briefly with the promotion's own 24 Hour Championship before losing it during that November's 12 Days Tournament.
note: Qualifiers, in order won: Justin Harper and Johnny Freil (Firestorm 09-12-03); Yancy Kilpatrick, Pandora and Daniel Sinz (Firestorm 09-24-03). Yancy "Y2K" Kilpatrick won the five-man final at Vegas Violence III by submission over Johnny Freil, then lost the title to Daniel Sinz by submission (Millennium Deathlock) on Day Five of the 12 Days Tournament (21 November 2003), after Sinz attacked him with a chair before the bell.

name: VWF Hardcore Championship
caption: A hardcore title Gods Tears proposed to majority owner Kingston Cash on Holiday Havoc II and won at his own off-page GT's Invitational, first billed on New Years Kick Off.
epitaph: A hardcore-rules title of the promotion's final months: Gods Tears proposed it to majority owner Kingston Cash on Holiday Havoc II and was first billed as its champion on New Years Kick Off (19 January 2005), the deciding bout having taken place off the page; its record runs only as far as the surviving broadcasts.

name: VWF Triple Threat Championship
notes: Named in the promotion's own 2001 cards as the Triple Threat Title, shortened on air to the T3 Title.
epitaph: A title decided and defended in three-way matches. G-Gangsta won the first one in August 2001 and held it into October, when Zell Strife took it; in November Strife handed the belt to Thomas Rainka, who defended it to the year's end.

name: BWF Championship
notes: The title of the Beautiful Wrestling Federation, Ric Beauty's faction inside the VWF, first awarded on 3 October 2001.
epitaph: The belt Ric Beauty created for his Beautiful Wrestling Federation faction, diamond and jewel encrusted, and awarded to Corey Fuller in a match he refereed himself. G-Gangsta took it from Fuller three weeks later; by December it was Classy Joey Boy's, with the faction's new president, Sebastian, demanding it back.

name: RAW-Vegas BlackJack Championship

events.note: Unified with the T3 Title at Ghosts of RAW; the winner became Vegas Heavyweight Champion.
events.title: vwf-vegas-2003-heavyweight

epitaph: The promotion's hardcore title of 2002. Classy Joey Boy had held it since December 2001 apart from one week in Tai Angela's hands, his latest reign running from February 2002, and defended it in a ladder match at Vegas Violence II and a steel cage at Phear Phantastic II; at Ghosts of RAW it was unified with the T3 Title into the Vegas Heavyweight Championship.
notes: Renamed from the BWF Championship on 10 January 2002, when Ric Beauty sold his stake in the BWF back to Rob Beauty on air and Classy Joey Boy continued as champion under the new name.

name: RCW Championship
notes: Crowned by the RCW, an invading faction of former outside wrestlers (G-Gangsta, Demonic, Blaze and the Real Deal) inside the VWF in January 2002; the broadcast itself questions whether the VWF recognizes it as an official title.
epitaph: A belt the RCW invaders crowned for themselves rather than one the promotion handed out. G-Gangsta won it in a four-way on 17 January 2002 by outlasting Demonic, Blaze and the Real Deal, then defended it in a Last Man Standing match through three tables and a bloody 2 out of 3 falls brawl through the streets of an old Nevada ghost town that left both men and the referee knocked out.
